title: Why We Need Sleep
summary: We spend about a third of our lives asleep. What is the body doing during all those hours?
paragraphs: If you live until you are ninety, you will spend about thirty years of your life asleep. For a long time, people thought that sleep was simply a time when the body and brain switched off and rested. Today, scientists know that this is not true. While we sleep, our bodies are very busy.

One of the most important jobs of sleep is to help the brain store memories. During the day, we learn many new things. At night, the brain sorts this information. It keeps what is useful and moves it into long-term memory. In one study, students who slept after learning a list of words remembered far more of them the next day than students who stayed awake.

Sleep also cleans the brain. When we are awake, waste products slowly build up between brain cells. During deep sleep, the space between the cells becomes larger, and liquid washes the waste away. Some scientists think this may help protect us from certain illnesses when we are older.

The body uses sleep to repair itself, too. Muscles grow and heal, and the body produces substances that help us fight infections. This is why people who do not sleep enough often get colds more easily.

So how much sleep do we need? Most adults need between seven and nine hours a night. Teenagers need even more, about eight to ten hours. However, many people get much less. Late-night screens are one common reason. The blue light from phones and computers tells the brain that it is still daytime, which makes it harder to fall asleep.

Not sleeping enough has clear effects. After just one bad night, people find it harder to concentrate, make more mistakes and feel more emotional. Over many months, a lack of sleep can increase the risk of serious health problems.

Experts suggest a few simple habits for better sleep. Go to bed and get up at the same time every day, even at weekends. Keep your bedroom dark, quiet and cool. Avoid coffee in the afternoon, and put your phone away at least an hour before bed. Sleep is not wasted time. It is one of the best things you can do for your body and your mind.

questions.question: What did people use to believe about sleep?
options: The brain works harder at night
The body and brain simply switch off
questions.explanation: For a long time people thought the body and brain simply switched off and rested.

questions.question: What happened in the study with the list of words?
options: Students who stayed awake remembered more
questions.explanation: Students who slept after learning remembered far more words the next day.

questions.question: Why do people who do not sleep enough get colds more easily?
options: Sleep helps the body fight infections
questions.explanation: During sleep the body produces substances that help us fight infections.

questions.question: Why do screens make it harder to fall asleep?
options: Blue light tells the brain it is still daytime
They make the room too warm
People get angry reading the news
questions.explanation: The blue light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the experts' suggestions?
options: Keep the bedroom dark and cool
Go to bed at the same time every day
questions.explanation: Experts suggest the same times every day, even at weekends, so sleeping longer at weekends is not a suggestion.

grammar.explanation: We use the first conditional for a real or likely situation and its result.
grammar.example: If you live until you are ninety, you will spend about thirty years of your life asleep.

exercise.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you will sleep more, you feel better.
If you sleep more, you will feel better.
If you slept more, you will feel better.
If you sleep more, you felt better.
exercise.explanation: First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb.

grammar.explanation: We can make a comparative stronger with far or much before it.
grammar.example: In one study, students who slept after learning a list of words remembered far more of them the next day than students who stayed awake.

exercise.question: Choose the correct option: Teenagers need ___ sleep than adults.
exercise.explanation: We use much (or far) before a comparative: much more.
